articles.headline: Master Plan lays ground for skyscrapers in Delhi
articles.summary: Delhi's Master Plan 2047 introduces a regulatory framework for taller buildings exceeding 100 floors by increasing density and floor area ratios. The plan aims to accommodate a projected population of 32 million by 2047, removing height restrictions in several construction categories and focusing development along mass-transit corridors to curb urban sprawl.

articles.headline: Lucknow man kills wife at work, shoots sister, himself dead
articles.summary: A 37-year-old bank employee in Lucknow shot dead his estranged wife outside her office and later killed his sister before committing suicide. The man, identified as Manas Bajpayee, reportedly confessed to the killings in a WhatsApp status message, citing betrayal. Police have recovered the bodies and are investigating the domestic dispute.

articles.headline: MP’s son driving Aston Martin kills woman, booked
articles.summary: The son of Rajya Sabha MP M Ramesh was booked for a hit-and-run incident in Hyderabad that killed a 26-year-old woman. Lingamaneni Sunjush allegedly struck the victim while driving a high-speed Aston Martin. The accused has been charged under BNS sections for causing death by negligence. Police are investigating the speed and circumstances of the crash.

articles.headline: S.I.T. to re-examine police probe in Ram temple case
articles.summary: A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed to investigate alleged irregularities in the police probe of a donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram Temple. The move follows Supreme Court observations regarding gaps in the initial investigation. Officials may re-examine criminal conduct that previously resulted in the arrest of eight people.

articles.headline: 6-yr-old Vizag boy dies after teacher slaps him
articles.summary: A six-year-old student at a private school in Visakhapatnam died after allegedly being slapped by a teacher for not completing homework. CCTV footage appears to show the teacher slapping the child before he collapsed. While the school rushed him to a hospital, he was declared dead on arrival. Local authorities have initiated an inquiry and a case has been registered.

articles.headline: New 3-judge apex court bench to hear PMLA review
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has constituted a new three-judge bench to hear review petitions challenging various provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The bench will re-examine the validity of powers granted to the Enforcement Directorate regarding arrests and searches, addressing concerns over potential misuse of the law's stringent provisions.

articles.headline: Farmlands face 49% rain deficit despite late spells
articles.summary: Agricultural regions in India continue to face a significant 49% rainfall deficit despite recent late monsoon spells. The shortage has impacted kharif crop sowing in several states, particularly hitting pulses and oilseeds. The weather department warned that the deficit could lead to reduced yields if major growing belts do not receive adequate precipitation in the coming weeks.

articles.headline: Wide mandate for July 20 probe panel
articles.summary: The Supreme Court-appointed committee to probe allegations of violence during the July 20 protests will have a broad mandate to investigate police conduct and systemic failures. The panel, led by a former judge, will examine the legality of police surveillance, use of force, and the role of anti-social elements. It aims to ensure accountability and prevent future escalations.

articles.headline: 2 vessels with 22 Indians on board hijacked
articles.summary: Pirates hijacked two commercial vessels carrying a total of 22 Indian nationals off the coasts of Yemen and Somalia. The tankers, MT Sibul and MV Luluf, were seized in separate incidents within the Gulf of Aden. Indian authorities are coordinating with international maritime agencies to ensure the safe release of the crew members and the vessels.

articles.headline: Top court refines ‘industry’ test but protects pending disputes
articles.summary: In a 5:4 majority ruling, the Supreme Court refined the decades-old 'industry' test while protecting pending disputes from the impact of the new formulation. The judgment aims to clarify what constitutes an 'industry' under the Industrial Disputes Act, ensuring that current legal proceedings continue under the existing framework to avoid mass disruption in labor litigation.

articles.headline: 3 Cong-ruled states to move SC against mines law
articles.summary: Governments of Karnataka, Kerala, and Telangana are set to challenge the new Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act in the Supreme Court. The states argue that the law unconstitutionally restricts their power to impose mineral-related levies. They claim the central legislation infringes upon state fiscal autonomy and financial interests.

articles.headline: South CMs talk water, delimitation with Shah
articles.summary: Chief ministers from southern states discussed critical issues including water sharing and parliamentary delimitation during a meeting chaired by Home Minister Amit Shah. The leaders expressed concerns over potential loss of representation due to population-based delimitation. They also sought central intervention to resolve inter-state water disputes involving the Cauvery and Godavari rivers.

articles.headline: HC stays Soren govt order cancelling JPSC exam
articles.summary: The Jharkhand High Court stayed a government order that cancelled the 11th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examination. The court provided interim relief to approximately 400 successful candidates whose recruitment was stalled by the cancellation. The stay follows petitions alleging the government's decision was arbitrary and lacked proper legal justification.

articles.headline: UGC equity rules under review; Centre tells SC
articles.summary: The Centre informed the Supreme Court that the University Grants Commission's (UGC) 2026 regulations on promoting equity in higher education are currently under review. The regulations had been kept in abeyance since January following petitions challenging their lack of specific definitions for 'caste-based discrimination'. The court has requested a formal affidavit from the government.

articles.headline: Govt hands over illegal drug racket case to SIT
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has ordered a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe a racket involving the repackaging and relabeling of expired drugs. The decision followed raids on an unauthorized facility in Bengaluru where counterfeit medicines of reputed brands were found. The six-member team will investigate the network's financial transactions and distribution channels.

articles.headline: ‘State to recommend rejection of draft on Kasturirangan report’
articles.summary: The Karnataka government will recommend the rejection of the draft notification on the Kasturirangan report concerning Western Ghats conservation. Minister Ramalinga Reddy cited concerns from local residents and farmers regarding restrictions on infrastructure and development. The state plans to officially convey its opposition to the Union environment ministry within 60 days.

articles.headline: Stir intensifies in Cauvery basin over release of water
articles.summary: Protests have intensified in Karnataka's Cauvery basin following the release of water from the Krishnaraja Sagar (KRS) dam to Tamil Nadu. Farmers and local activists held demonstrations, citing inadequate water levels for local irrigation. The state government is managing the release under directives from the Cauvery Water Management Authority despite local opposition.

articles.headline: HC reserves order on Siddaramaiah, DKS defamation plea
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court has reserved its order on a petition by CM Siddaramaiah and Deputy CM D.K. Shivakumar seeking to quash a defamation case. The case involves an advertisement issued by the Congress party during the 2023 elections alleging corruption by the then BJP government. The court heard arguments regarding the nature of political advertising and public interest.

articles.headline: No cases of foreigners getting Aadhaar: Min
articles.summary: The Karnataka government informed the state legislature that there are no verified cases of illegal immigrants, including Pakistanis or Bangladeshis, obtaining Aadhaar cards in the state. The home minister clarified that while some FIRs were filed against individuals for possessing forged documents, none have been confirmed as foreigners illegally receiving government-issued IDs.

articles.headline: Three F.I.R.s over unauthorised posters of Min
articles.summary: Bengaluru police registered three FIRs against unidentified individuals for putting up unauthorized posters of a state minister on public walls. The posters were found in several locations across the city without the mandatory permissions. Authorities have initiated an investigation to identify those responsible for the defacement of public property and violation of local bylaws.

articles.headline: Officials crack down on illegal chemical banana ripening units
articles.summary: A health department team in Udupi district raided several warehouses and seized 5,000 kg of raw bananas being ripened using hazardous chemicals. The operation targeted units using calcium carbide and artificial coloring agents. Authorities warned vendors against these practices, which pose serious health risks to consumers. Legal action has been initiated against the facility owners.

articles.headline: Expired goods, fungal growth found at railway station eateries
articles.summary: Food safety inspections at several major railway stations in Karnataka revealed the sale of expired products and fungal growth in food items. Teams checked 112 food establishments, including those at Bengaluru City and Yeshwanthpur stations. Several vendors were fined for unhygienic conditions and the use of non-permitted food colors. The reports will be sent to railway authorities.

articles.headline: Assembly passes 3 bills amid Oppn protest
articles.summary: The Karnataka Assembly passed three key bills, including the Bangalore Development Authority (Amendment) Bill 2026, amid loud protests from the opposition. Opposition members were demanding the resignation of a minister over alleged corruption. The new laws aim to regularize certain unauthorized properties and streamline land acquisition processes in Bengaluru.

articles.headline: Row erupts as Vijay seeks govt ‘assurance’ over delimitation
articles.summary: A political row broke out in Tamil Nadu after actor-politician Vijay urged the Centre for a 'clear legislative assurance' against any reduction in the state's parliamentary representation due to delimitation. Vijay's statement came during a party meeting where he emphasized that population-based seat reallocation could unfairly penalize states with effective family planning.

articles.headline: Shah seeks backing of states to combat drugs
articles.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah urged southern states to support the Centre's three-year roadmap to make India drug-free by 2047. Speaking at the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting, Shah emphasized the need for better coordination between state and central agencies to disrupt international drug trafficking networks and enhance rehabilitation efforts for addicts.

articles.headline: 4 of family killed in T'gana as car falls into well
articles.summary: Four members of a family died when their car veered off the road and fell into an open well in Telangana's Dubbak mandal. The victims, including a two-year-old child, were traveling home after attending a local festival. Police reported that the driver likely lost control of the vehicle due to poor visibility and lack of a protective wall around the well.

articles.headline: Jagan challenges CM to order CBI probe into APPSC exams
articles.summary: YSR Congress president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy challenged the Andhra Pradesh CM to order a CBI investigation into alleged irregularities in APPSC Group-I examinations. Jagan denied any wrongdoing during his tenure and accused the current government of attempting to malign his administration. He stated that a central probe would reveal the transparency of the selection process.

articles.headline: Telangana Cong issues notice to leaders over ‘anti-CM’ statements
articles.summary: The Telangana Congress Committee issued show-cause notices to several party leaders for making 'anti-party' and 'anti-CM' remarks. The move aims to enforce party discipline following public criticisms of the CM's policies. The leaders have been asked to respond within three days, failing which they may face disciplinary action or suspension from the party.

articles.headline: Pocso court awards pastor 4 death sentences for sexual assault
articles.summary: A special POCSO court in Tirunelveli awarded four death sentences to a 47-year-old pastor for the sexual assault of four minor girls. The court found the accused guilty of multiple counts of aggravated sexual assault between 2022 and 2023. In addition to the death penalty, the court imposed a fine of ₹20 lakh on the convict to be paid to the victims' families.

articles.headline: Kerala child rights panel seeks transparency in contest judging
articles.summary: The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights directed authorities to ensure transparency in judging school arts festivals. The commission ordered that marks awarded by judges be displayed on electronic screens immediately after performances. This directive aims to prevent allegations of bias and corruption in the evaluation of student competitions.

articles.headline: TN announces initiatives to modernise consumer, food protection systems
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government announced 24 initiatives to modernize its food and consumer protection systems, including the introduction of AI-based monitoring and QR-coded bags. The plan includes constructing 13 new warehouses to increase storage capacity for the public distribution system. The initiatives aim to reduce food wastage and ensure better supply chain management across the state.

articles.headline: Bleaching powder purchase gaps to be probed: Kerala min
articles.summary: Kerala health minister Veena George ordered a detailed probe into alleged irregularities in the purchase of bleaching powder by the state's medical services corporation. The move follows reports of overpricing and quality issues in recent procurement rounds. The minister stated that any official found guilty of financial negligence would face strict action.

articles.headline: Modi calls for greater youth engagement by government
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged government departments to create more platforms for youth engagement and internships. During a meeting with top secretaries, he emphasized the need to incorporate fresh perspectives from young professionals in policy-making. The PM suggested that every ministry should aim to train and mentor students to build a more dynamic bureaucracy.

articles.headline: Nvidia to ship AI chip for China by year-end
articles.summary: Nvidia plans to start shipping small volumes of a new AI chip designed specifically for the Chinese market by the end of the year. The chip complies with recent US export controls while meeting the growing demand for AI hardware in China. This move aims to maintain Nvidia's presence in one of the world's largest semiconductor markets despite ongoing trade restrictions.

articles.headline: 50 killed after boat capsizes in Nigeria
articles.summary: At least 50 people, including many children, died after an overloaded boat capsized in northwestern Nigeria. The vessel was carrying more than 100 people when it overturned in a river. Rescuers have recovered several bodies, and search operations continue for missing passengers. Local authorities cited overcrowding and poor maintenance as the primary causes of the disaster.

articles.headline: Rupee exports get equal footing with dollar, euro
articles.summary: The government has amended the Foreign Trade Policy to allow export benefits for transactions settled in Indian rupees, putting them on par with those in US dollars or euros. This move aims to promote the internationalization of the rupee and reduce dependence on foreign currencies for trade. Exporters will now be eligible for incentives even for rupee-denominated earnings.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi suggests 4 steps for states in edu sector
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi recommended four key steps for Congress-ruled states to improve the education sector, including a state-level scholarship for meritorious students and a robust system to prevent paper leaks. He emphasized the need for modernizing infrastructure and ensuring timely recruitment of teachers. These suggestions follow recent controversies over national-level entrance examinations.

articles.headline: Mere mention of caste no offence under SC/ST Act, rules HC
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court ruled that merely mentioning a person's caste does not constitute an offense under the SC/ST Act unless it is done with the intent to humiliate. The court quashed an FIR where the accused had used a caste name during a dispute without any evidence of derogatory intent. The judgment emphasizes that the law's primary purpose is to prevent targeted harassment.

articles.headline: FIRs against 35 of 87 quashed in Sept 2025 violence in Leh
articles.summary: Ladakh authorities have quashed FIRs against 35 individuals out of 87 originally charged in connection with violent protests in Leh in September 2025. The decision followed a review by a special committee which found insufficient evidence for criminal prosecution against these individuals. The move is seen as an effort to restore normalcy and address community grievances in the region.

articles.headline: Mehul Choksi's lawyer arrested in London on sexual assault charges
articles.summary: Vijay Aggarwal, a senior lawyer representing fugitive businessman Mehul Choksi, was arrested in London on multiple counts of sexual assault. London police stated that the charges involve four separate incidents. Aggarwal has been remanded in custody following his initial court appearance. His legal team in India has yet to issue a formal statement regarding the allegations.

articles.headline: U.P. BEOs prohibit YouTubers' entry into schools
articles.summary: Education officers in Uttar Pradesh have issued orders prohibiting the entry of YouTubers and social media influencers into government schools without prior permission. The move aims to prevent unauthorized filming of students and disruption of academic activities. Authorities cited concerns over privacy and the spread of misinformation through unverified video content.

articles.headline: 45 projects to explore critical minerals in Bastar cleared
articles.summary: The Chhattisgarh government has cleared 45 projects for the exploration of critical minerals, including lithium and graphite, in the Bastar region. The exploration will be carried out over the next two years to identify potential mining sites. This initiative is part of India's strategic push to secure domestic supplies of minerals essential for green energy and high-tech industries.

articles.headline: Structures near visa section of Pak high commission removed
articles.summary: Delhi municipal authorities removed several unauthorized structures and encroachments near the visa section of the Pakistan High Commission. The action was taken citing security concerns and the need for public passage clearance in the high-security diplomatic enclave. The removal process was completed under police protection and did not involve any diplomatic buildings.

articles.headline: HC steps in after CRPF deployed in tense Shillong
articles.summary: The Meghalaya High Court has intervened following the deployment of CRPF personnel in Shillong to manage communal tensions. The court has directed the state government to provide daily status reports and ensure that civilian rights are protected during the security operations. The deployment followed recent clashes that prompted authorities to impose a temporary curfew in certain areas.

articles.headline: SC: Police can’t file FIR under Pre-natal Act
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that police cannot independently register an FIR or investigate offenses under the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act. The court clarified that only authorized officers specified under the Act can file complaints before a magistrate. This judgment aims to prevent the misuse of police powers and ensure compliance with the Act's procedures.

articles.headline: Dusty hydrants, dead detectors: Inside Kolkata's fire-trap hotels
articles.summary: An investigation into several budget hotels in Kolkata revealed severe fire safety violations, including non-functional smoke detectors and rusted fire hydrants. Many establishments lacked proper emergency exits and fire extinguishers. Local municipal authorities have issued show-cause notices to several hotel owners, warning of potential closures if safety standards are not met.

articles.headline: HC questions Centre on delay over same-sex medical rights
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court questioned the central government over its delay in recognizing medical rights for same-sex partners in live-in relationships. The court emphasized the need for a legal framework that allows partners to make medical decisions for each other in emergencies. The Centre has been asked to file a comprehensive response addressing these civil rights concerns within four weeks.

articles.headline: Hooch tragedy toll rises to 7 in Guj, 13 arrested
articles.summary: The death toll from a hooch tragedy in Gujarat's Bhavnagar district has risen to seven, with several others still hospitalized in critical condition. Police have arrested 13 people suspected of producing and distributing the illicit liquor. The state government has ordered a high-level inquiry to identify lapses in law enforcement and prevent future occurrences of similar tragedies.

articles.headline: 4 killed as trucks collide in HP tunnel
articles.summary: Four people were killed and several others injured when two trucks collided inside a tunnel on the Hanogi-Jhalogi highway in Himachal Pradesh. The crash occurred due to poor visibility and brake failure in one of the vehicles. Authorities had to block the tunnel for several hours to clear the wreckage. An investigation has been launched into the safety protocols of the tunnel stretch.

articles.headline: Disabled man pushed to death from Mumbai local
articles.summary: A 62-year-old physically challenged man died after being allegedly pushed out of a moving Mumbai local train following an argument over seating. Police have arrested the suspect, who reportedly engaged in a scuffle with the victim before the incident. The Railway Police are reviewing CCTV footage from the station to gather more evidence for the murder investigation.

articles.headline: A bolder India on China border
articles.summary: An editorial analysis suggests that India is adopting a more assertive stance on its border with China, focusing on infrastructure development and enhanced military presence. The piece argues that while dialogue remains open, India is prioritizing strategic readiness to prevent further territorial incursions. The shift reflects a long-term strategy to ensure national security along the LAC.

articles.headline: What Gor did not say in Kashmir
articles.summary: This opinion piece examines recent statements made by a US diplomat during a visit to Kashmir, highlighting omissions regarding regional autonomy and human rights. The author suggests that international diplomatic rhetoric often avoids the complex ground realities of the region. The article calls for a more nuanced international engagement that addresses the aspirations of local residents.

articles.headline: Trump may escape the consequences of his mess
articles.summary: An editorial column discusses the potential for Donald Trump to evade legal and political accountability for recent controversies. The author analyzes the current political climate in the US and how it may favor Trump's return to power despite ongoing investigations. The piece warns of the implications for American democratic institutions if institutional checks fail to hold him accountable.

articles.headline: All of us should have the right to age with dignity
articles.summary: This opinion piece advocates for better social security and healthcare systems for India's aging population. It highlights the challenges faced by the elderly in accessing affordable care and the need for a national policy that ensures dignity in old age. The author suggests that as the demographic shifts, the government must prioritize geriatric care and financial support for seniors.

articles.headline: IndiGo’s transition plan has one risk too many
articles.summary: A business analysis explores IndiGo's strategy to expand its international operations and the potential risks involved in fleet transitions. The piece notes that while the airline aims to dominate long-haul routes, operational complexities and global fuel price volatility could impact its profitability. The author suggests that a more cautious approach might be needed to maintain market leadership.

articles.headline: North Korea may have up to 120 nuclear weapons
articles.summary: A new intelligence report suggests that North Korea may have expanded its nuclear arsenal to as many as 120 warheads. The estimate follows recent satellite imagery of increased activity at North Korean nuclear facilities and several successful missile tests. International experts expressed concern over the rapid growth of the program and its implications for East Asian security.

articles.headline: Germany: 14,000 heat-related deaths in summer
articles.summary: Germany reported more than 14,000 heat-related deaths this summer, marking one of the deadliest seasons on record. Authorities attributed the high mortality rate to prolonged heatwaves and inadequate cooling infrastructure in many cities. The government has pledged to invest in 'heat-resilient' urban planning and public health awareness campaigns to mitigate future climate-related risks.

articles.headline: 2 Khalistan supporters warned by Canada police about threat
articles.summary: Canadian police have officially warned two prominent Khalistan supporters that their lives may be in danger due to potential assassination plots. The individuals, involved in recent referendums, were advised to take extra security precautions. This warning comes amid heightened tensions between India and Canada following allegations of targeted killings of activists on Canadian soil.

articles.headline: NASA mission to rescue satellite ends in failure
articles.summary: NASA's high-profile mission to rescue a malfunctioning communication satellite has ended in failure after the rescue craft failed to dock successfully. The mission aimed to extend the satellite's life by five years through on-orbit servicing. Despite the setback, NASA officials stated that the technology tested during the attempt would be used to improve future robotic satellite maintenance.

articles.headline: India Inc’s Q1 performance conceals a widening divide
articles.summary: Corporate India's Q1 results reveal a growing gap between large, resilient firms and smaller companies struggling with rising costs. While major industry leaders reported double-digit profit growth, many MSMEs faced declining margins due to higher interest rates and weak domestic demand. Analysts suggest that a broad-based recovery may take longer as small businesses continue to underperform.

articles.headline: Bonds recover as US Treasury comes to rescue
articles.summary: Global bond markets recovered significantly after a US Treasury buyback program helped stabilize yields and boost investor confidence. The move followed weeks of volatility in the debt market, which had impacted equity prices. Analysts noted that the intervention provided much-needed liquidity, although concerns over long-term inflation and interest rate hikes remain in the market.

articles.headline: Nearly 72% petrol pumps fall under open category
articles.summary: A government report indicates that nearly 72% of petrol pumps in India now fall under the 'open category', allowing for greater private sector participation. This shift follows recent deregulation policies aimed at increasing competition and improving service quality in the fuel retail sector. Private players have seen their market share grow as they expand their networks across urban and rural areas.

articles.headline: Sindhu’s valiant stand ends in agony as pairs shine
articles.summary: PV Sindhu's quest for a historic world championship title ended in a hard-fought quarter-final loss to Wang Zhi Yi. Despite winning the first set, Sindhu couldn't maintain the momentum as her opponent rallied back. However, Indian doubles pairs, including Satwik-Chirag, continued their winning streak, advancing to the next round with dominant performances in their respective matches.

articles.headline: India Open locked in winter window despite criticism
articles.summary: The Badminton World Federation has decided to keep the India Open in its current January time slot despite concerns over Delhi's severe winter pollution. International players had expressed health concerns following high AQI levels during previous tournaments. The BWF stated that a lack of alternative dates in the global calendar made a rescheduling difficult for the 2027 season.

articles.headline: India-born Ishika charts her own path in badminton
articles.summary: Ishika Jaiswal, an India-born badminton player representing the US, is making waves on the international circuit with several recent tournament victories. Jaiswal, who moved to the US as a child, credited her Indian roots for her tactical discipline and rigorous training. She aims to break into the world's top 20 and represent her adopted country at the next Olympics.

articles.headline: Root and Cox hit 50s, England reaches 239/4
articles.summary: Joe Root and Jordan Cox struck impressive half-centuries to guide England to a solid 239/4 on the opening day of the first Test against Pakistan. The duo shared a century partnership, stabilizing the innings after early wickets. Despite some tight bowling from Pakistani pacers, England's middle order maintained a steady run rate, putting the team in a strong position by stumps.

articles.headline: Resilient India hold England, advance to second round
articles.summary: The Indian women's hockey team played out a resilient goalless draw against England to advance to the second round of the World Cup. India's defense, led by goalkeeper Savita Punia, withstood several penalty corners to ensure the crucial point. The result ensures India stays in the top two of their group, keeping their hopes of a podium finish alive as they head into the knockout stages.

articles.headline: The veteran and his understudy: Rahul-Padikkal partnership
articles.summary: KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal's 165-run partnership was the highlight of India's opening day in the Test series against Sri Lanka. The veteran Rahul provided stability while the young Padikkal displayed aggressive stroke-play, confusing the Sri Lankan bowlers. Their partnership rescued India from early trouble and has been hailed as a potential blueprint for the team's future middle order.

articles.headline: Neeraj-Pathirage battle set for Lausanne Diamond League
articles.summary: Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra is set to face fierce competition from Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage at the upcoming Lausanne Diamond League meet. Both athletes have consistently cleared the 88m mark this season, making them top contenders for the title. Fans are expecting a high-intensity javelin throw competition as Neeraj looks to secure another gold and maintain his world ranking.

articles.headline: Maresca, City and the shadow of Guardiola
articles.summary: Manchester City's new manager Enzo Maresca faces the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola as the team begins its Premier League title defense. Analysts have noted similarities in their tactical approaches, but Maresca has emphasized his desire to build his own identity at the club. The article explores whether Maresca can maintain City's dominance while stepping out of Guardiola's shadow.

articles.headline: Refs boss Webb wants monitoring of set-piece fights
articles.summary: Howard Webb, the head of referees for the Premier League, has called for stricter monitoring of player scuffles during set-pieces. Webb stated that excessive grappling and time-wasting in the penalty area would result in more yellow cards this season. The move aims to improve the flow of the game and reduce controversial VAR decisions related to minor infractions during corners and free-kicks.

articles.headline: GST Council likely to review rate rationalisation in upcoming meeting
articles.summary: The GST Council is scheduled to meet on Saturday to discuss various issues, including rate rationalisation and the review of the 28% tax on online gaming. This first meeting under the new government is expected to set the tone for future tax reforms and provide relief for specific sectors to boost the economy.

articles.headline: Finance Ministry considers increasing standard deduction for individual taxpayers
articles.summary: The Finance Ministry is reportedly considering a proposal to provide tax relief to individual taxpayers in the upcoming Union Budget. Potential changes include an increase in the standard deduction or adjustments to income tax slabs under the new tax regime, aimed at boosting disposable income and middle-class consumption.

articles.headline: Nvidia becomes world's most valuable company as AI rally continues
articles.summary: Nvidia has overtaken Microsoft to become the world's most valuable publicly traded company. Its market cap reached $3.33 trillion, fueled by the explosive demand for its AI chips. This surge underscores the dominant role of artificial intelligence in current market trends and the massive growth potential of the high-performance computing sector.

articles.headline: NEET-UG paper leak controversy sparks nationwide protests and political row
articles.summary: Protests have erupted across India following allegations of paper leaks and irregularities in the NEET-UG 2024 medical entrance examination. The Education Ministry has sought a report from the Bihar Police regarding the matter. Opposition parties are demanding a high-level probe, while students and parents call for a re-examination to ensure fairness.

articles.headline: International Day of Yoga celebrations planned across various historic Indian sites
articles.summary: The Indian government has finalized preparations for the 10th International Day of Yoga on June 21. Major events are scheduled at historic locations, with the Prime Minister leading celebrations in Srinagar. The event aims to promote global health and wellness through yoga, with millions expected to participate worldwide.

articles.headline: Delhi government approaches Supreme Court over worsening water shortage crisis
articles.summary: The Delhi government has approached the Supreme Court seeking an urgent direction to Haryana for the release of additional water. The national capital is suffering from a critical water shortage during a peak heatwave, leading to restricted supply and public protests. The petition highlights the humanitarian crisis caused by depleting reservoir levels.

articles.headline: Rising cases of heatstroke reported across North India due to extreme heat
articles.summary: Hospitals in Delhi and surrounding regions have reported a significant surge in heatstroke cases as temperatures hover near 45 degrees Celsius. Health authorities have issued advisories urging people to stay hydrated and avoid outdoor activities during peak hours. Special clinics have been set up to manage the influx of patients.

articles.headline: Extreme heatwave persists in North India as monsoon progress stalls
articles.summary: North India continues to face record-breaking temperatures as heatwave conditions persist for the fourth consecutive week. Meanwhile, the southwest monsoon has hit a plateau, delaying much-needed relief to the northern plains. The delay is impacting agricultural preparations and straining the power grid due to increased demand.

articles.headline: Opposition parties coordinate strategy for upcoming stormy Parliament session
articles.summary: Leading opposition parties have convened to coordinate their parliamentary strategy against the government for the upcoming session. Key points of contention include the NEET exam irregularities and the relocation of historic statues in the Parliament complex. The alliance aims to present a united front on issues of public concern.

articles.headline: Government plans massive investment in national highway projects this fiscal
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways plans to award road projects worth Rs 2 lakh crore this fiscal year. The initiative focuses on finishing existing expressways and starting new greenfield corridors to enhance logistics. This massive investment aims to boost economic growth and improve connectivity across major industrial hubs.

articles.headline: US Fed signals single interest rate cut for current year
articles.summary: The US Federal Reserve has indicated that it expects only one interest rate cut in 2024, despite cooling inflation. Policymakers noted that while progress has been made toward their 2% goal, the economy remains strong. The decision has significant implications for global markets and central banks, including the Reserve Bank of India.

articles.headline: Sebi approves new framework to curb finfluencer activity in markets
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has approved a new framework to regulate financial influencers. The move is aimed at curbing the spread of misleading financial advice. Regulated entities are now prohibited from associating with unregistered persons who provide investment advice or claim specific returns to investors.

articles.headline: Air India Express to increase flights on domestic routes this season
articles.summary: Air India Express has announced plans to expand its domestic network by adding new frequencies on several key routes. The airline aims to capture a larger share of the summer travel demand and improve connectivity between Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities. This expansion is part of the ongoing integration process under the Tata Group.

articles.headline: Study finds rising microplastic contamination in global water sources
articles.summary: A new study reveals rising microplastic contamination in global water sources, with particles found in major rivers and oceans. The research warns that these particles are entering the human food chain through water and seafood. Scientists are calling for urgent global policy changes to reduce plastic production and improve waste management.

articles.headline: India defeats Afghanistan in T20 World Cup Super Eight stage
articles.summary: The Indian cricket team secured a convincing victory over Afghanistan in their first Super Eight match of the T20 World Cup. Stellar performances by the batsmen and a disciplined bowling attack ensured a comfortable win. The victory puts India in a strong position to qualify for the semi-finals of the global tournament.

articles.headline: Former SC Judge Reddy to Lead Probe into CJP March Action
articles.summary: Former Supreme Court judge R Subhash Reddy will head a five-member enquiry committee to probe alleged police excesses on students marching to Parliament on July 20. The panel will examine if police used excessive force and will check the validity of sedition law usage. The committee includes former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and former Meghalaya DGP L R Bishnoi.

articles.headline: Fake Drugs Bypassing Retail Chain Discovered by Bengaluru Chemists
articles.summary: Bengaluru's drug regulatory body found that spurious and counterfeit medicines are bypassing licensed retail pharmacies. These fake drugs, often used in ICUs for critical care, are being supplied directly to hospitals through intermediaries or online sellers. Chemists claim this shadow supply chain evades the checks established in retail pharmacies, risking patient safety.

articles.headline: Gandhi Manuscript Fetches Record ₹16.2 Crore at Auction
articles.summary: A handwritten manuscript containing Mahatma Gandhi's daily thoughts, written over 23 months for his disciple Anand T Hingorani, sold for ₹16.2 crore ($1.7 million). The 688-page archive set a world record for an Indian historical document. The collection, which includes reflections and photos, was purchased by an Indian bidder at a Saffronart auction.

articles.headline: Six Indians Among Crew Hijacked by Somali Pirates
articles.summary: A Cameroon-flagged cargo ship with six Indian crew members was hijacked by Somali pirates in the Gulf of Aden. The vessel was reportedly carrying weapons when it was seized. This incident follows a recent surge in piracy in the region. Authorities and international maritime forces are monitoring the situation to secure the release of the crew and the ship.

articles.headline: Imported Firearms Seized from Bandipur Farmhouse Hint at Poaching
articles.summary: Police seized modern, sophisticated firearms, including a US-made SG552-2 Commando rifle and high-velocity ammunition, during a raid on a farmhouse near Bandipur Tiger Reserve. The seizure of high-end foreign weapons and animal remains like deer antlers suggests a well-organised poaching syndicate. Authorities are hunting for the absconding farmhouse owner and his associates.

articles.headline: Karnataka Government Admits Lack of Data on Local App-Cab Drivers
articles.summary: The Karnataka government revealed in the legislative council that it has no specific data on how many of the 2 lakh active app-cab drivers in Bengaluru are locals. While aggregators like Uber and Ola account for 75,000 drivers, the government admitted that many drivers are from neighboring states. New rules will require drivers to have local residency and knowledge of Kannada.

articles.headline: Heavy Rains and Weekend Rush Paralyse Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road
articles.summary: A combination of pre-festival shopping, heavy rains, and ongoing metro work reduced traffic on Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road to a crawl. Commuters reported travel times of over three hours for distances normally covered in 30 minutes. The situation highlights the city's struggling infrastructure, particularly in tech corridors where waterlogging has become a chronic issue.

articles.headline: FDA Raids Railway Eateries, Finds Serious Hygiene Violations
articles.summary: A special Food and Safety Drug Administration inspection at railway station eateries in Bengaluru and Hubballi revealed major hygiene breaches. Violations included the use of non-permitted colors in food and the use of newspapers to pack snacks like vadas and samoas. Authorities found expired ingredients and unhygienic preparation conditions, leading to immediate fines and warnings.

articles.headline: India to Import 10 Lakh Tonnes of Sugar Amid Shortage
articles.summary: For the first time in a decade, the Indian government has allowed the import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar to stabilize domestic prices. The move comes as opening stocks fell to a 20-year low, and sugar production is projected to decline by 20% this season. The imports aim to ensure adequate availability during the upcoming festive season and prevent a sharp rise in retail costs.

articles.headline: Seven Drug Overdose Deaths in One Week in Punjab
articles.summary: Punjab's Malwa region recorded seven drug overdose deaths in a single week, involving victims aged 16 to 45. The fatalities occurred in Bathinda and Mansa districts. Local police have arrested multiple alleged drug traffickers and recovered various narcotics. The surge in deaths has sparked fresh concerns over the deepening drug crisis and the circulation of high-potency synthetic drugs.

articles.headline: CJI Kant Urges Experts to Streamline Three-Language Education Policy
articles.summary: Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud and Justice S Kant called for a panel of experts to review and streamline the three-language policy in schools. The court noted the policy has become a colonial relic and needs to include indigenous languages while balancing the use of English and Hindi. The bench suggested providing extra assistance to students struggling with the linguistic transition.

articles.headline: Government to Amend Investment Treaty to Attract Global Players
articles.summary: The Centre is set to amend the model bilateral investment treaty (BIT) to include international arbitration in place of the current 'exhaustion of local remedies' clause. The change aims to provide greater legal certainty to foreign investors and boost FDI. Under the new rules, investors can seek international arbitration after one year of domestic litigation instead of five.

articles.headline: Sebi Study Shows Big Firms Profit at Retail Traders' Expense
articles.summary: A Sebi study revealed that large proprietary firms and prop traders accounted for nearly 80% of total profits in the Futures and Options (F&O) segment. In contrast, individual retail traders suffered collective losses of over ₹91,000 crore in FY26. The findings highlight a significant wealth transfer from small investors to institutional players who use sophisticated algorithmic tools.

articles.headline: WhatsApp Bans Over 3.7 Crore Indian Accounts in Six Months
articles.summary: WhatsApp reported banning more than 3.7 crore Indian accounts between January and June 2026 to combat spam and harmful activity. The platform used automated detection systems to proactively identify and block suspicious accounts. This volume of bans marks a significant increase compared to previous years, reflecting stricter enforcement of community guidelines and user safety protocols.

articles.headline: US National Debt Hits Historic Milestone of $40 Trillion
articles.summary: The US national debt has crossed the $40 trillion mark, driven by high government spending and rising interest rates. The debt has increased by roughly $8.5 trillion since 2020. Economists warn that the ballooning debt-to-GDP ratio, now exceeding 110%, could lead to higher inflation and reduced global trust in the US dollar if fiscal discipline is not implemented by the next administration.

articles.headline: Australia Passes Law Forcing Tech Giants to Pay for News
articles.summary: The Australian parliament passed legislation that forces global tech giants to pay local media outlets for displaying their news content. Companies failing to reach commercial agreements could face heavy fines. The law aims to support the domestic journalism industry, which has seen declining advertising revenue. Similar models are being considered by other nations to regulate big tech.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Citizens Hug Ancient Rock to Stop Tunnel Project
articles.summary: Hundreds of protesters formed a human chain at Lalbagh to protect a 3.3-billion-year-old Peninsular Gneiss rock from a proposed 17km tunnel project. Citizens fear the underground drilling will damage the park's fragile ecosystem and water table. The Lalbagh Walkers' Association has urged the government to find alternative routes for the Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel to preserve the heritage site.

articles.headline: Rare Genetic Disorder Found in 8-Year-Old Girl in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Doctors at IGICH, Bengaluru, have identified a rare genetic disorder in an eight-year-old girl who weighs only 8kg and stands 81cm tall. The condition, linked to a mutation in the MADD gene, causes severe developmental delays and stunted growth. This is the first reported case of this specific genetic defect in India, providing new insights into rare endocrine and neurological diseases.

articles.headline: BDA Bill Passed to Halve Regularisation Charges for Layouts
articles.summary: The Karnataka assembly passed the Bangalore Development Authority (Amendment) Bill, which halves the regularisation charges for unauthorized houses in BDA layouts. The move will benefit over 11 lakh residents by making it easier to obtain valid property documents for sites up to 4,000 sq ft. The amendment also allows for the regularisation of corner sites at revised, more affordable rates.

articles.headline: SEBI curbs cool derivatives market as individual traders lose ₹91,685 crore
articles.summary: SEBI's measures to curb excessive speculation in equity derivatives coincided with individual investors' net losses rising to ₹91,685 crore in FY26. Active individual traders fell 20% to 78.6 lakh, the first decline since FY16. Despite fewer traders, the average net loss per person rose to ₹1.17 lakh, with 90.9% of loss-making traders continuing to stay active despite financial setbacks.

articles.headline: SBI expands cash withdrawal charges to all basic savings bank accounts
articles.summary: State Bank of India expanded withdrawal charges for basic savings bank deposit (BSBD) accounts to plug fee income leaks. From October 1, customers with basic accounts opened via branches get four free monthly withdrawals, after which ₹15 plus GST applies. Digital transactions and withdrawals at ATMs of other banks remain free to encourage the use of self-service channels.

articles.headline: Private hospitals oppose parliamentary panel call to link room rents to CGHS
articles.summary: Private hospitals are opposing a parliamentary panel's suggestion to link room rents to CGHS or average hotel rates in the vicinity. Hospitals argue the move ignores high operating costs and rising service expenses. Healthcare CEOs stated that hospital charges include medical care, nursing, and infrastructure costs, making them incomparable to standard hotel room rents.

articles.headline: Gold prices surge 2% on US Treasury bond buyback program expansion
articles.summary: Gold prices surged nearly 2% to ₹1,57,080 per 10g in Mumbai following the US Treasury's plan to double its bond buyback program to $4 billion per operation. The move boosted investor interest in bullion as 30-year US Treasury yields dropped from near two-decade highs. Silver also rose sharply by ₹8,541 to ₹2,37,766 per kg in the same session, reflecting strong physical demand.

articles.headline: Premium bikes and scooters drive export growth for Indian two-wheeler makers
articles.summary: Two-wheeler exports are shifting towards premium segments, with bikes above 200cc growing at 12.8% and scooters at 18.2% during FY22-FY26. Indian brands like Royal Enfield, Bajaj Auto, and TVS Motor are expanding their presence in mid-capacity segments across global markets. Overall two-wheeler exports reached 5.18 million units in FY26, with premium models leading the surge.

articles.headline: India prepares to release gene-edited rice varieties to boost stagnant yields
articles.summary: India is set to release two gene-edited rice varieties, DRR Dhan 100 and Pusa Rice DST1, for commercial cultivation this rabi season. Developed using CRISPR/Cas9, these varieties offer higher yields and improved drought/salt tolerance compared to conventional strains. The move aims to address stagnant rice productivity and climate challenges while reducing reliance on water and fertilizers.

articles.headline: Tata Trusts delay in holding AGMs raises questions over legal recourse
articles.summary: Delay in holding AGMs for Sir Ratan Tata Trust and Navajbai Ratan Tata Trust has raised legal questions over the trusts’ finances and leadership. The delay caused an estimated opportunity cost of ₹56 lakh on ₹2,900 crore in deferred receipts. Issues involve potential legal remedies and the impact of the Charity Commissioner's expanded powers over internal functioning and trustee rights.

articles.headline: India and Japan agree to safeguard vital undersea communication cables
articles.summary: India and Japan agreed to safeguard undersea communication cables and strengthen maritime security in the Indo-Pacific. Defense Minister Rajnath Singh and Japanese counterpart Minoru Kihara discussed deepening cooperation in naval shipbuilding and technological exchange. The move targets threats to vital sea lines of communication and ensures protection of undersea infrastructure.

articles.headline: India open to buying Venezuelan oil pending US sanction exemption status
articles.summary: India remains open to buying Venezuelan crude oil as long as US sanction exemptions continue and prices are favorable. In August, Venezuela was India's fourth-largest supplier, providing 444,000 barrels per day. Reliance Industries and Nayara Energy are major importers, seeking to diversify sourcing and reduce reliance on West Asian oil as domestic demand for heavy crude remains high.

articles.headline: Indian exports to Australia surge 200% as CECA talks expand trade
articles.summary: Indian exports to Australia surged over 200% in five years, reaching nearly $30 billion. Both nations are exploring a broader Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) to include services, digital economy, and movement of people. Current trade is supported by the existing Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA), which has significantly boosted agriculture and auto exports.

articles.headline: India should aspire for growth beyond 7.5% per cent: RBI Deputy
articles.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Michael Patra stated India should aspire for growth beyond the current 7.5% rate, citing the economy's resilience to global shocks. He noted that India's current account deficit is expected to decline significantly. India received $95 billion in FDI last year, and Patra believes future inflows could reach $150 billion annually as the nation moves toward a developed status.

articles.headline: SEBI and RBI pursue bond tokenisation pilot for faster market settlement
articles.summary: SEBI and RBI are pursuing a pilot project for bond tokenisation to enable faster settlement and automated coupon payments. Whole-Time Member Amarjeet Singh stated the project aims for simultaneous transfer of securities and funds via shared data. The move is expected to improve efficiency in the corporate bond market and enhance liquidity by automating manual back-office processes.

articles.headline: SEBI plans trading reforms to reverse FPI outflows and boost weight
articles.summary: SEBI plans to introduce reforms including cash equity and longer-dated derivatives to boost the Indian stock market's weight in global indices and reverse FPI outflows. Proposed changes aim to ease entry for foreign investors and improve market liquidity. The reforms come as India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index fell below 12%, prompting a focus on institutional investor needs.

articles.headline: Southern States are main pillars of India's growth, says Amit Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah described Southern States as the main pillars of India's growth at the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting. He called for early resolution of long-pending inter-state water disputes and coordinated action against drugs and organized crime. Shah noted that India cannot reach a $10 trillion economy without the progress and contribution of all southern states.

articles.headline: DGFT eases rupee trade regulations to support Indian exporters globally
articles.summary: The DGFT has eased regulations to allow Indian exporters to invoice and settle international trade in rupees. Exporters can now receive export incentives and fulfill obligations for trade settled in Indian currency. The move aims to promote the internationalisation of the rupee and reduce dependence on the US dollar for global settlements, specifically targeting trade with Asian nations.

articles.headline: Trump warns countries helping Iran of severe economic consequences
articles.summary: US Presidential candidate Donald Trump warned of economic consequences for any country or entity providing a lifeline to Iran. Trump's comments aim to divert public opinion from domestic financial problems and increase pressure on Tehran. He stated that any financial institution or business assisting Iran will face tremendous economic consequences as part of his strategy to isolate the regime.

articles.headline: India and Singapore discuss key economic ties in ISMR meeting
articles.summary: India and Singapore discussed strengthening economic ties in manufacturing, semiconductors, and digital technology during the ISMR meeting. Ministers from both sides focused on the 'six pillars' of cooperation, including green economy and skills development. Two MoUs were signed on food safety and digital connectivity between UPI and PayNow to facilitate easier cross-border transactions.

articles.headline: Bitcoin tops $70,000 as US Treasury Secretary backs national reserve
articles.summary: Bitcoin surpassed $70,000 for the first time in two months, driven by US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen’s support for a national crypto reserve. The surge was also fueled by declining US bond yields and increased institutional interest. Bitcoin rose 4.5% to over $72,000, while ether and other major tokens also posted gains, wiping out significant short positions in the derivatives market.

articles.headline: ESIC adds 4,961 doctors to India's national healthcare pool
articles.summary: The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) added 4,961 doctors to the national pool, including 1,200 specialists. ESIC is expanding its medical education facilities with nearly 880 seats for MBBS and 559 for postgraduate courses across its colleges. The initiative aims to provide quality healthcare to beneficiaries through 169 medical institutions and hundreds of regional offices.

articles.headline: CBI to coordinate with States to plug GST evasion in mining
articles.summary: The CBI will coordinate with state authorities to curb GST evasion in illegal mining by sharing intelligence and monitoring mineral movements. The initiative follows CAG reports highlighting significant revenue loss due to non-payment of taxes on illegal mineral transport. Authorities will use e-way bills and vahan data to track and plug leaks in the tax collection system for minerals.

articles.headline: IndiGo tests 20% of pilots annually for substance abuse: CEO
articles.summary: IndiGo CEO Pieter Elbers announced the airline tests 20% of its pilots annually for substance abuse, double the DGCA's 10% mandate. The airline has strengthened SOPs to manage flight disruptions and improved crew management. Despite a ₹2,393 crore net loss in FY26 due to fuel prices and grounded aircraft, IndiGo aims for sustainable growth while ensuring the highest safety standards.

articles.headline: Delhi-NCT to ban diesel and petrol light goods vehicles from 2027
articles.summary: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) will ban diesel, petrol, and CNG-powered light goods vehicles (LGVs) in Delhi-NCT from January 1, 2027. The move aims to reduce vehicular emissions and transition transport to electric vehicles. In the NCR districts of Gurugram and Faridabad, the ban will take effect from July 2028, reflecting a phased approach to air pollution control.

articles.headline: Premium petrol demand triples due to E20 ethanol blend concerns
articles.summary: Consumer demand for premium, high-octane petrol has surged threefold to 12-15% of sales from 4% in March, as motorists fear E20 ethanol-blended fuel could damage vehicle mileage and engine life. Despite E20 also containing 20% ethanol, higher octane is believed to mitigate adverse effects. Industry executives expect demand for Octane 95 to keep rising unless ethanol-free options are provided.

articles.headline: Banks struggle to deploy FCNR dollar influx after RBI's early closure
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's early closure of the FCNR(B) deposit scheme has caused a rapid influx of dollars, leaving banks scrambling to deploy funds. This could lead to negative carry and push up borrowing costs. Banks face legal and procedural hurdles to raise funds overseas within the shortened timeline, potentially disrupting financial planning and asset-liability management.

articles.headline: RBI proposes new rules to regulate fintech small loans, pricing
articles.summary: RBI has floated draft rules to standardize loan pricing for fintechs and restrict NBFCs to term loans. The proposals aim to address opaque pricing and coercive recovery practices in app-based lending, bringing NBFC pricing closer to bank frameworks. While protecting borrowers from high APRs, it could reduce credit access for "thin-file" customers, particularly for microfinance and personal loans under ₹50,000.

articles.headline: India faces sugar scarcity due to rising ethanol demand
articles.summary: India's increased ethanol-fuel blending program is driving up sugarcane demand, leading to rising sugar prices and potential scarcity. The government has imposed stock limits on bulk buyers and is considering sugar imports for the first time in nearly a decade. This trade-off between fuel blending and food prices highlights a need for market-model testing and review of the blending program.

articles.headline: Women's agricultural work undervalued, faces unequal access
articles.summary: Despite women comprising 64% of India's agricultural workforce, their contribution remains under-recognized, often classified as unpaid labor (47.7%). They earn 82 paise for every ₹1 earned by men and face lower access to credit and inputs, resulting in 24% lower productivity. This unequal access leads to an estimated ₹1.2-2 trillion (2.5-4% of total output) forgone annually.

articles.headline: India pushes for harmonized administrative data for better policy
articles.summary: India is systematically working to harmonize vast troves of government administrative data across ministries and states. By adopting metadata standards, quality frameworks, and common classifications, disparate data-sets (e.g., Ayushman Bharat IDs, e-Shram portal, Udyam portal) can be made interoperable. This aims to unlock insights for policymaking and service delivery, ensuring privacy with the DPDP Act.

articles.headline: Nuclear power expansion unlikely to reduce India's electricity bills
articles.summary: India aims for 100GW nuclear capacity by 2047, but high capital costs (₹14-30 crore/MW) and long construction times (8-9 years) make new nuclear power tariffs uncompetitive (₹7.77-7.88/unit) against falling renewable energy costs (₹5.25/unit). The government may need to offer fiscal support and revisit tariff determination for private sector confidence and to achieve carbon compliance goals.

articles.headline: India's rural job guarantee scheme weakened, employment generated falls
articles.summary: India's rural employment guarantee program, MGNREGA, has been repealed and replaced by VB-G RAM G, which shifts 40% of costs to states. Employment generated fell sharply to 76.7 million person-days in July, compared to 391 MPD in July 2020 and 153 MPD in July 2025. This weakening comes amid a 13% monsoon deficit and stagnant real wages, risking deeper rural distress.

articles.headline: RBI maintains hawkish tone on inflation risks despite stable rates
articles.summary: RBI policymakers struck a hawkish tone in August meeting minutes, warning of lingering inflation risks from food and fuel shocks, despite keeping the repo rate at 5.25%. While 69% of weighted CPI basket saw 4% or less inflation in June, 28% of CPI items recorded above 4% inflation in July, signaling a shift towards higher inflation pressures.

articles.headline: India's exports surge in July, led by US, Singapore, Malaysia, Japan
articles.summary: India's exports grew across key markets in July 2026. The US remained the top destination (20.4% share), with shipments up nearly 13% y-o-y. Exports to Singapore (83.7%), Malaysia (73%), Japan (65.3%), and China (64.6%) saw strong double-digit growth. Top 10 markets accounted for over half of overall exports, but rising commodity prices may inflate values.

articles.headline: Skymet raises drought probability to 70% as monsoon weakens
articles.summary: Private weather agency Skymet revised its 2026 monsoon forecast to 85% of LPA, raising drought probability to 70% from 30% in April, citing a strengthening El Niño. Rainfall was 13% below LPA over June-July, and August-September are expected to be deficient. A weak monsoon could hurt kharif yields, rural incomes, water availability, and raise food prices.

articles.headline: Rural women drive sharp increase in India's labour force participation
articles.summary: India's labour force participation rate (LFPR) among those aged 15+ rose sharply in July, primarily driven by rural women whose LFPR jumped 220 basis points to 38.8% from June. Urban female LFPR also rose slightly to 25.3%, while male LFPR remained broadly stable in both rural and urban areas.

articles.headline: FPIs return to Indian equities, led by consumer services and healthcare
articles.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) accelerated their return to Indian equities in July, extending June's recovery after a prolonged sell-off. Consumer services attracted the highest inflows ($1.06 billion), followed by healthcare ($0.81 billion) and consumer durables ($0.77 billion). Capital goods, telecom, and auto sectors saw the largest outflows.

articles.headline: Centre's Green India Mission achieved only 2% of forest cover target
articles.summary: The Centre's Green India Mission fell 98% short of its forest cover target between FY16 and FY25, adding only 0.03 million hectares against a 1.4 million-hectare goal, according to a CAG report.

articles.headline: IT ministry approves ₹7,877 crore investment for electronics manufacturing
articles.summary: The IT ministry approved ₹7,877 crore investment for 31 projects under the first tranche of its ₹40,000-crore Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme.

articles.headline: Cabinet approves ₹13,041 crore for four railway quadrupling projects
articles.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved ₹13,041 crore investment for four railway track-quadrupling projects on the Howrah-Chennai network and a highway project in Bihar.

articles.headline: India plans ₹10,000 crore investment for new national waterways
articles.summary: India plans a ₹10,000 crore investment over 5-10 years to develop over a dozen new national waterways, expanding the operational network into viable cargo and passenger corridors.

articles.headline: Health ministry frames rules for hair transplant clinics after fatalities
articles.summary: The health ministry has finalized SOPs for hair transplant clinics to curb botched procedures, complications, and fatalities at salon-like facilities. New guardrails mandate qualified medical staff (postgraduate degrees in plastic surgery, dermatology, ENT, general surgery, or maxillofacial surgery with trichology training), surgical-grade facilities, and emergency preparedness. Non-compliance faces penalties up to ₹5 lakh and prosecution.

articles.headline: Automation reshapes IT job pyramid, firms adjust hiring strategies
articles.summary: Automation is forcing India's largest IT firms to restructure their employee pyramids. Seven of the top 10 IT companies have announced changes: some (Cognizant, Tech Mahindra, Sonata) aim to broaden the junior base, others (Wipro, LTM, Coforge) to expand the middle, while TCS focuses on skill-based structures. This means pressure on freshers to quickly develop skills.

articles.headline: Bar Council faces backlash over student protest, powers questioned
articles.summary: The Bar Council of India (BCI) faced widespread condemnation and a legal challenge after attempting to halt Nalsar's 2026 batch enrollment over a student protest. The episode, quickly withdrawn, sparked deeper questions about BCI's powers, accountability, electoral process, and lack of representation for young lawyers, with calls for reforms to its regulatory authority.

articles.headline: Government urges uniform farm financing for contract farming
articles.summary: The government asked public sector banks and the IBA to develop standard loan products and uniform documentation for contract farming within 6-12 months. This aims to ease financing for aggregators and first-stage processors, basing lending decisions on buyer reliability rather than collateral. It includes a model tripartite agreement and proposals for custom hiring centers.

articles.headline: India, EU finish legal scrubbing of trade pact text for signing
articles.summary: India and the 27-nation European Union have completed the legal scrubbing of their free trade agreement text, aiming for signing this year on a mutually agreed date.

articles.headline: Indian Oil finalizing LPG import deal with Algeria's Sonatrach
articles.summary: Indian Oil Corp. (IOC) is finalizing a deal with Algeria’s Sonatrach to import liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) in 2027. India is diversifying LPG sources to reduce reliance on West Asia following the Strait of Hormuz blockade. IOC will lift 45,000-55,000 metric tonnes of LPG monthly.

articles.headline: India diversifies crude supply, increases Venezuela imports
articles.summary: India is expanding its crude oil sourcing to Latin America, increasing imports from Venezuela in August due to disruptions linked to the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz. Venezuela is now India’s fourth-largest supplier.

articles.headline: Delhi plans 4 million new homes by 2047 under new master plan
articles.summary: Delhi plans to build 4 million new homes and evenly spread its population as it prepares for an additional 8 million residents by 2047. These targets are part of the national capital’s new Master Plan, unveiled by Union housing and urban affairs minister Manohar Lal.

articles.headline: India's battery storage self-reliance a decade away due to component gap
articles.summary: India will take another 10 years to achieve self-sufficiency in battery storage due to a significant gap between demand and current capability to manufacture essential battery cell components, according to a Wood Mackenzie report. This leaves India dependent on imports.

articles.headline: India has costliest rocket launches globally, impacting space ambitions
articles.summary: India's satellite launch costs are the highest among global space powers at $13,302 per kg, over four times the US figure. This high cost could challenge India's private space industry and its ambition to capture 8% of the global market. Experts urge lowering costs to compete with the EU and Japan.

articles.headline: D2C startup funding bar rises as investors demand higher revenue
articles.summary: India's D2C ecosystem maturity means investors are raising revenue thresholds for startup funding, from seed to later rounds. Easier distribution via e-commerce and quick commerce makes topline growth less valuable without repeat purchases, healthy unit economics, and clear profitability. Funding for D2C mid-stages fell from $416 million to $280 million in H1 2026.

articles.headline: Trump threatens Iran with 'Economic D-Day' amid Gulf tensions
articles.summary: President Trump vowed to unleash "ECONOMIC D-DAY" on Iran, targeting any country providing a "lifeline" to the regime through financial institutions, businesses, or airports. This follows weeks of cajoling the UAE to curb Iranian financial networks, which then suspended transactions. The move aims to grind down Iran economically amid escalating tensions and an expired agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Retail F&O losses moderate in FY26, but frequent traders still bleed
articles.summary: Individual equity derivatives traders incurred ₹91,685 crore in losses in FY26, down from ₹1.12 trillion in FY25, according to a Sebi study. However, the average loss per trader rose by 2% to ₹1.17 lakh. 87.7% of traders lost money, with frequent traders (100+ days active) generating 94% of turnover and 87% of total losses, averaging ₹2.76 lakh.

articles.headline: Swiggy's Instamart to adopt inventory-owned model for profitability
articles.summary: Swiggy's quick commerce arm, Instamart, will adopt an inventory-owned model after Swiggy became an Indian-owned and controlled firm, reducing foreign ownership to 49.5%. This shift is expected to improve profitability, with Ebitda margin potentially rising 80-100 bps, despite current losses. Instamart's net order value grew 39% y-o-y in Q1FY27, with losses narrowing.

articles.headline: MRF faces margin pressure from rising costs and high valuation
articles.summary: Tyre maker MRF expects increased margin pressure in FY27 due to surging raw material costs. Q1FY27 revenue rose 10% y-o-y, but Ebitda dropped 8%, with gross margins down 570 bps. Analysts warn of 8-10% raw material cost rise in Q2FY27. MRF stock trades at an expensive 20x estimated FY28 earnings, making it vulnerable to input cost changes and competition.

articles.headline: Sebi adjudication proceedings fall to decade low in FY26
articles.summary: Adjudication proceedings by market regulator Sebi fell to a decade low of 135 in FY26 from 204 a year ago, reflecting stronger compliance systems and a targeted enforcement approach. The number of orders against registered intermediaries declined to 88. Violations involving fraudulent trade practices still accounted for the most orders.

articles.headline: Mutual funds favor large-caps as FPIs reduce mid and small-cap exposure
articles.summary: Mutual funds increased holdings in nearly two-thirds of large- and mid-cap companies in Q1FY27, driven by strong domestic equity inflows. Conversely, Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) cut holdings in a majority of companies across all market caps. This shift shows FPIs influenced by global allocation, while MFs receive steady household savings.

articles.headline: IndiGo achieves record 67.4% market share in July as rivals slip
articles.summary: India's largest airline, IndiGo, reached a record 67.4% domestic market share in July, while Akasa Air's share fell to 5.5% and SpiceJet's to 1.6%. The overall domestic aviation market contracted 5% y-o-y and 11% sequentially in July, due to airlines cutting capacity amid a surge in jet fuel prices triggered by the West Asia war.

articles.headline: IndiGo CEO prioritizes A350 induction for profitable overseas expansion
articles.summary: IndiGo's new CEO, William Walsh, identified the Airbus A350 induction as key for profitable overseas expansion, aiming to boost international flights to 40% of capacity by FY30. With 60 A350-900s on order from next year, IndiGo targets long-haul routes to the US, Canada, Australia, and Europe, seeking to capture traffic currently dominated by foreign carriers while maintaining cost advantage.

This expansion is driven by a surge in road construction and airport development in smaller towns, boosting demand for travel and hospitality. The company expects to cross the 100-hotel mark by end of 2026.

articles.headline: Indian firms' Q1 earnings recovery shows widening divide
articles.summary: Indian companies delivered a stronger-than-expected 18% y-o-y profit growth in Q1FY27, but the recovery showed a clear divide: large and mid-sized firms pulled ahead with double-digit revenue and profit growth, benefiting from commodity upcycle and credit growth. Smaller firms struggled with higher costs and weaker pricing power, seeing only 5% profit growth, highlighting uneven profit quality.

articles.headline: Traditional banks increase startup lending as new economy matures
articles.summary: Traditional banks are expanding into startup lending as more new-age businesses achieve profitability and steady cash flows, offering cheaper credit. articles.headline: Hero MotoCorp's electric CV bet Euler Motors scales rapidly
articles.summary: Hero MotoCorp's investment in Euler Motors, an electric commercial vehicle company, is scaling rapidly, doubling sales and revenue, and adding manufacturing capacity. Euler’s sales grew 87% to 6,528 units in FY26 and 5,318 units in first four months of FY27, prompting capacity expansion.

articles.headline: Bollywood stars embrace niche filmmakers, experimental projects

articles.headline: LinkedIn becomes accidental dating site despite no-romance rules
articles.summary: Despite strict no-romance guidelines, LinkedIn is increasingly used for dating, as singles are exhausted by traditional dating apps. While the platform alerts users to profile views, some craft network-focused messages to initiate connections.

articles.headline: Kuwait braces for prolonged Iran conflict, recalling past traumas
articles.summary: Kuwait, facing drone strike damage and heightened tensions with Iran, is recalling past traumas (like the 1991 Iraqi invasion) as it navigates the protracted Gulf conflict. The ongoing conflict intensifies its historical struggle to manage external threats from larger neighbors.

articles.headline: Luxury sales plunge in China as tax push hits affluent shoppers
articles.summary: Luxury sales in China dropped over 10% in July for 25 biggest brands, worse than June, reversing an earlier recovery. This slump coincides with China's clampdown on offshore wealth and tighter tax controls, dampening spending by the wealthy. LVMH, Kering, and Hermès saw double-digit drops, as affluent Chinese shift money to stocks and face depressed property values.

articles.headline: India's reservoir storage deficit narrows but remains below last year
articles.summary: India's reservoir storage deficit narrowed due to monsoon rains, with live storage at 59.4% of combined capacity, up from 28.5% a month ago in the central region. However, storage remains 19.6% below last year's level across most regions, underscoring continued pressure on water resources. The western region is the only one above last year's level.

articles.headline: Ind-Ra keeps neutral outlook for transport infrastructure sector in FY27

articles.headline: Tata Consumer Products targets double-digit revenue growth in FY27

articles.summary: India eased rules on rupee export payments, aligning them with foreign-currency earnings for trade-policy benefits.
